question: Can statistical structure observed across populations of trained MLP weights be reduced to a simple, learning-free initialization that accelerates training beyond standard zero-mean initialization?

key_findings.claim: The paper's empirically supported intervention is a nonzero mean in the first matrix of each two-layer MLP, not a general reconstruction of the trained joint weight distribution.
key_findings.evidence: For y = W2 sigma(W1 x), the paper presents a random row-broadcast offset W1' = W1 + 1_p b_n^T with b_n drawn from a zero-mean Gaussian (Eq. 1) and an even simpler deterministic scalar shift W1' = W1 + b 1_p 1_n^T (Eq. 2). It explicitly says that modifying W1's mean is its only empirically backed MLP finding so far.

key_findings.claim: The covariance study is unusually population-based but is confined to about ten thousand tiny models, so transfer of the observed stripes to the evaluated 22M-parameter model is an untested extrapolation.
key_findings.evidence: Rather than treating rows, columns, or filters inside one model as samples, the authors estimate the joint covariance of [vec(W1), vec(W2)] across roughly 10^4 independently trained CIFAR-10 networks. The ConvNeXts used for this estimate have only 3-4 layers, width about 16-32, MLP expansion 2, and a few thousand to about 10^4 parameters; no covariance estimate is reported for DeiT-Small.

anchors.section: Section 2 Understanding the Covariance Structure of Trained MLPs

key_findings.claim: A fixed scalar shift cannot reproduce the population covariance stripes that motivate it, contrary to the paper's wording.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 2 adds the same deterministic b to every W1 entry. Across random initializations, Cov(W_ij + b, W_kl + b) = Cov(W_ij, W_kl), so a fixed shift changes the first moment but creates no off-diagonal covariance. Equation 1 can create row-shared covariance because b_n varies by network; Eq. 2 would mimic a rank-one uncentered second moment only if the displayed statistic were not centered, or would mimic covariance if b were randomly sampled per network. Neither qualification is stated, while the paper says both strategies produce the Figure 1 stripes.

key_findings.claim: The visual covariance evidence is not quantified enough to establish which trained statistic the initialization actually matches.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 1 presents two covariance heatmaps and the text describes stripes, stronger structure in Cov(W1) than Cov(W2), and ViT cross-layer anticorrelation. It reports no covariance magnitude, eigenspectrum, confidence interval, population-centering convention, layer-to-layer variation, training-time evolution, or hypothesis test. The ViT panel is explicitly labeled 'enhanced; may need to zoom for structure.'

key_findings.claim: The observed ViT anticorrelation is a reported negative result, and the proposed subtraction is dimensionally underspecified under the paper's own matrix shapes.
key_findings.evidence: The paper observes apparent W1/W2 anticorrelation for the small ViT, not ConvNeXt, but reports no training benefit from anticorrelated MLP initialization. It writes W1' = (W1 - W2)/2 even though W1 is defined as p-by-n and W2 as n-by-p; a transpose or explicit vectorization alignment is required and is not given.

anchors.section: Section 2 / ViT covariance and negative anticorrelation result

key_findings.claim: On CIFAR-10 ConvNeXt, the MLP shift yields a clear early-epoch gain that is almost gone by 50 epochs, while convolutional mimetic initialization retains a larger benefit.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 averages five completed runs per epoch budget. From the plotted axis, MLP mimetic initialization is roughly 6 percentage points above uniform near epoch 5 and roughly 3 points above it near epoch 10, but all ConvNeXt curves converge near 94% by epoch 50. The paper explicitly says the MLP effect tapers while the convolutional mimetic effect remains.

key_findings.claim: On the tiny CIFAR-10 ViT, the MLP shift persists longer than on ConvNeXt but is much weaker than self-attention mimetic initialization.
key_findings.evidence: The ViT has dimension 192, depth 8, and 3 heads. Figure 2 shows the MLP-only curve about 2 percentage points over uniform at 10 epochs and about 1 point over it at 50 epochs, whereas the attention-mimetic and combined curves are roughly 8-9 points above uniform at 10 epochs and about 4 points above it at 50 epochs. Values are read approximately from a plot rather than supplied in a table.

key_findings.claim: The sole exact large-scale endpoint is a small ImageNet-1k improvement whose stated effect size is arithmetically inconsistent with the rounded accuracies.
key_findings.evidence: For DeiT-Small (22M parameters) trained for 100 epochs, the text reports 68.8% top-1 with the method and 68.4% for uniform initialization. That is a 0.4 percentage-point difference from the printed values, although the figure caption and prose call it a 0.5% advantage. The discrepancy could come from unreported unrounded values, but those values and uncertainty are absent.

key_findings.claim: The sign of the scalar shift is not important over the tested range; zero is the conspicuous local failure point.
key_findings.evidence: In a five-seed sweep from b = -0.1 to 0.1 on 10-epoch ConvNeXt-128/8 CIFAR-10 training, all plotted baselines dip at exactly b = 0 and recover on either side. The curves are about 0.85-0.86 at zero and about 0.88-0.89 for many nonzero settings, based on the graph. This supports a nonzero symmetry-breaking or activation-shift effect, not a learned preferred sign.

key_findings.claim: Simple bias controls do not explain the plotted gain, but the ablation does not identify the mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 includes default ConvNeXt initialization plus mimetic MLP, Kaiming-uniform plus mimetic MLP, two constant-initialized linear-bias controls (0.1 and 0.01), and a single learnable scalar bias implementing b sum(x) 1_p. All retain a dip at b = 0, and initializing the ordinary linear-layer bias to a small constant is also reported ineffective. No activation, gradient, conditioning, or optimization-path measurement distinguishes the remaining hypotheses.

anchors.section: Figure 4 and Is it really the init?

key_findings.claim: The reported ConvNeXt baseline is not the architecture's default initialization, which limits external comparability even though the within-figure comparison can remain matched.
key_findings.evidence: The authors replace ConvNeXt's truncated normal with standard deviation 0.02 and zero bias by PyTorch Kaiming uniform because this broadly improved their setup. Consequently, the 'uniform' baseline in the main experiment is an altered and apparently selected training recipe; the paper does not show a full crossed comparison of official default versus Kaiming, each with and without the proposed shift.

key_findings.claim: The method composes with spatial mimetic initialization, but the incremental effect becomes small when the stronger attention initialization is present.
key_findings.evidence: On ConvNeXt, the combined convolution-plus-MLP curve is best early and the text says it outperforms either mimetic initialization alone. On CIFAR-10 ViT and ImageNet-1k, the combined attention-plus-MLP curve is close to the attention-only curve; the authors explicitly characterize the additive ImageNet gain as 'rather small.'

key_findings.claim: Reproduction and causal interpretation are blocked by missing hyperparameters and training details.
key_findings.evidence: The paper does not state the b used in Figures 2-3, the sigma used for Eq. 1, which equation supplies each main curve, optimizer and learning-rate details, batch size, weight decay, full augmentation recipe, covariance-layer sampling rule, or ImageNet seed count. It has no appendix, tabulated main results, code link, or artifact statement.

key_findings.claim: The authors appropriately bound the result as preliminary and less robust than earlier mimetic work.
key_findings.evidence: The conclusion says there is only a small amount of preliminary evidence that Eq. 1 may be preferable at larger scale, explicitly calls for larger-scale research, and states that the results are not as robust as mimetic initialization for spatial mixing. It hypothesizes, rather than demonstrates, that the technique matters most in data-limited settings.

method.core_idea: Estimate joint MLP-weight statistics across many independently trained networks, interpret striped population covariance as shared row or column means, and initialize the first MLP matrix with a small shared offset.
method.mechanism: For an MLP y = W2 sigma(W1 x), begin with a conventional random W1. Equation 1 adds a Gaussian vector shared across all p rows, preserving zero global mean across a population while correlating entries in each broadcast group. Equation 2 instead adds one fixed scalar to every W1 entry, shifting preactivations by b times the sum of input coordinates. The latter is used as the extremely simple headline method. The intervention is combined independently with prior structured initializations for depthwise convolution or self-attention.
assumptions: Population covariance estimated from roughly 10^4 tiny CIFAR-10 networks captures structure that is relevant to substantially larger networks and ImageNet.
The striped heatmap reflects a causally useful trained-weight statistic rather than parameter symmetries, normalization, optimizer effects, or a low-level artifact of vectorization.
A shared row or column mean is the correct interpretation of the stripes even though no quantitative factor model is fitted.
A fixed scalar first-moment shift can stand in for a random, zero-mean population covariance component.
The sign of b need not match trained weights; only nonzero magnitude matters over the plotted sweep.
Adding b times the summed input to every hidden preactivation does not create harmful saturation or dependence on input centering in other modalities.
Normalization and Adam do not immediately erase the initialization effect.
Epoch-limited accuracy is an adequate measure of training speed without reporting examples, FLOPs, or wall-clock time.
The altered Kaiming-uniform ConvNeXt baseline is representative of standard practice and does not interact specially with b.
Five CIFAR seeds and an unstated ImageNet seed count adequately characterize a small effect.
The visually observed W1/W2 anticorrelation has a meaningful entry alignment despite transposed matrix shapes.
Short-run CIFAR-10 gains predict utility in genuinely data-limited learning even though dataset-size scaling is not tested.

techniques.role: Treats whole independently trained networks as samples when estimating the joint distribution of vec(W1) and vec(W2).
Adds a per-input-coordinate Gaussian vector shared across W1 rows to create within-group covariance while retaining zero population mean.
Adds a fixed scalar to every first-layer MLP weight as the simplest tested training intervention.
Converts a qualitative statistic of trained weights into a closed-form, learning-free initialization.
Applies the MLP shift alongside earlier convolutional or self-attention mimetic initializers.
Tests ordinary linear bias, a learnable shared scalar, and alternative base initializations as explanations for the effect.
Searches for dependence between W1 and W2 and reports anticorrelation in ViT but not ConvNeXt.

evaluations.setting: Approximately 10^4 tiny 3-4-layer ConvNeXts, width about 16-32 and MLP expansion 2, trained independently on CIFAR-10.
evaluations.result: Figure 1 shows visually striped within-matrix blocks, more pronounced for W1 than W2; no numerical covariance statistic or uncertainty is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Prior within-one-network row, column, or filter covariance analyses; no iid-initialization heatmap is shown in the figure.

evaluations.setting: Small ViT population trained with the same CIFAR-10 setup.
evaluations.result: The enhanced heatmap is described as showing the same stripes plus W1/W2 anticorrelation; the strength is not quantified.
evaluations.baseline: Tiny ConvNeXt population, where the cross-layer anticorrelation is not observed.

evaluations.setting: Isotropic ConvNeXt-256/8 with 7x7 depthwise filters on CIFAR-10, 2x2 patches, RandAugment, five seeds per completed epoch budget.
evaluations.result: The MLP curve is approximately 6 points over uniform near epoch 5 and 3 points over it near epoch 10, but the curves are nearly tied around 94% by epoch 50; values are plot-read because no table is supplied.
evaluations.baseline: Kaiming-uniform initialization, convolutional mimetic initialization, and convolution-plus-MLP mimetic initialization.

evaluations.setting: Tiny ViT with dimension 192, depth 8, 3 heads, 2x2 CIFAR-10 patches, five seeds per epoch budget.
evaluations.result: MLP initialization is approximately 72% versus 70% uniform at 10 epochs and approximately 85% versus 84% at 50 epochs; attention mimetic and combined variants reach approximately 79% at 10 and 88% at 50.
evaluations.baseline: Uniform, attention-mimetic, and attention-plus-MLP mimetic initialization.

evaluations.setting: DeiT-Small, 22M parameters, 16x16 patches at 224x224, ImageNet-1k, Touvron et al. training pipeline, 100 epochs.
evaluations.result: 68.8% with the reported MLP method versus 68.4% uniform at 100 epochs; the printed endpoint difference is 0.4 percentage points even though the text calls it 0.5%.
evaluations.baseline: Uniform initialization and self-attention mimetic initialization, alone and combined with the MLP shift.

evaluations.setting: ConvNeXt-128/8 on CIFAR-10 for 10 epochs, scalar b swept from -0.1 to 0.1, five seeds per b.
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy mean and standard deviation.
evaluations.result: Every plotted recipe has a local minimum at b = 0; accuracy is roughly 85-86% at zero and commonly 88-89% for nonzero b. Exact point values are not tabulated.
evaluations.baseline: Default ConvNeXt base initialization, Kaiming uniform, constant ordinary biases initialized to 0.1 or 0.01, and a single learnable bias.

evaluations.setting: ConvNeXt CIFAR-10 short-duration training with two independently applicable structured initializers.
evaluations.result: Convolution-plus-MLP mimetic initialization is reported to outperform either alone early; only the convolutional contribution remains clearly separated at long duration.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 tiny ViT and ImageNet-1k DeiT-Small with two mimetic initializers.
evaluations.result: The MLP initializer adds a visible early benefit, but its incremental contribution over attention-mimetic initialization is described as smaller on CIFAR and rather small on ImageNet.
evaluations.baseline: Attention mimetic initialization without the MLP shift.

evaluations.setting: Small ViT MLPs with an initialization intended to reproduce observed W1/W2 anticorrelation.
evaluations.baseline: The nonzero-W1-mean initializer, which does improve early training.

evaluations.result: A learnable shared scalar and small constant initialization of the ordinary linear bias do not absorb or reproduce the nonzero-weight-mean effect.
evaluations.baseline: Directly shifting every W1 weight by nonzero b.

limitations: Author-stated: the MLP effect is much smaller and less robust than prior mimetic initialization for spatial mixing layers.
Author-stated: the advantage decreases with training duration and nearly disappears for ConvNeXt by 50 epochs.
Author-stated: evidence that the random zero-global-mean Eq. 1 is better at larger scale is preliminary, and more large-scale research is needed.
Author-stated: W1/W2 anticorrelation is observed in ViT but not ConvNeXt and gives no measured initialization benefit.
Reviewer-identified: a deterministic global shift does not change centered population covariance, so Eq. 2 does not mathematically mimic the motivating stripes as claimed.
Reviewer-identified: Figure 1 supplies qualitative heatmaps but no numerical covariance strength, eigenspectrum, confidence interval, centering convention, or layerwise stability analysis.
Reviewer-identified: the covariance population uses tiny CIFAR models and is not re-estimated on the 22M-parameter DeiT-Small where transfer is claimed.
Reviewer-identified: the paper never states the b used for Figures 2-3, sigma for Eq. 1, or which equation generates each main curve.
Reviewer-identified: optimizer, learning rate, batch size, weight decay, full augmentation, covariance sampling, and ImageNet seed count are absent.
Reviewer-identified: there is no appendix, code link, raw result table, or artifact statement.
Reviewer-identified: main ConvNeXt experiments replace the architecture's default truncated-normal initialization with Kaiming uniform after observing broad improvement.
Reviewer-identified: the rounded ImageNet values imply +0.4 percentage points, not the stated +0.5%.
Reviewer-identified: the W1-minus-W2 expression is dimensionally invalid without a transpose or vectorization convention.
Reviewer-identified: CIFAR plot values are not tabulated, forcing approximate visual extraction and preventing precise effect-size checks.
Reviewer-identified: there is no dataset-size sweep despite the specific hypothesis that the method matters in data-limited regimes.
Reviewer-identified: the evaluation covers only image classification, two architecture families, and at most one modest ImageNet recipe.
Reviewer-identified: no activation saturation, gradient norm, Hessian, signal propagation, conditioning, or feature-learning measurement explains the effect.
Reviewer-identified: accuracy per epoch is called speedup without measuring wall-clock time, examples processed, or compute overhead.
Reviewer-identified: modern learned and architecture-specific initialization methods are not used as baselines.
Reviewer-identified: selecting b by a sweep can itself consume more tuning than the paper's 'compute-free' initialization framing acknowledges.
failure_modes: The early advantage washes out with sufficient ConvNeXt training.
The incremental benefit can become negligible when a stronger self-attention mimetic initializer is already used.
Setting b exactly to zero returns the local accuracy dip seen across all Figure 4 recipes.
A large |b| may shift MLP preactivations into activation saturation or make behavior depend strongly on input centering; the tested range ends at 0.1.
Inputs whose coordinates sum near zero make the fixed shift contribute little because its functional effect is b times sum(x).
LayerNorm or other normalization placement may cancel or reshape the induced common-mode activation.
A deterministic b cannot reproduce random across-network covariance even if its training effect is positive.
Anticorrelating W1 and W2 does not help in the reported ViT trial.
Using an unspecified transpose/alignment for W1/W2 can make the anticorrelation initialization irreproducible.
The method may optimize a short-horizon transient without changing the final basin or generalization.
A b chosen on CIFAR may not transfer across width, expansion ratio, activation function, modality, or optimizer.
The apparent gain may interact with the selected Kaiming-uniform base recipe rather than hold across standard defaults.
Population covariance structure from tiny networks may disappear or change sign at practical scale.
The global mean shift may break desirable zero-mean signal-propagation assumptions in untested deep or normalization-free MLPs.
reusable_insights: Treat independently trained networks as statistical samples when within-model exchangeability is doubtful; this makes global parameter dependencies estimable.
Separate first-moment, centered-covariance, and uncentered-second-moment interventions explicitly before claiming that one mimics another.
A broadcast weight offset has a simple functional interpretation: it injects the input-coordinate sum as a common hidden feature.
Initialization gains should be plotted over training budget because large transient improvements can vanish at convergence.
Cross spatial-mixing and channel-mixing initializers factorially to test whether their gains are independent, redundant, or antagonistic.
Use both fixed-sign and random-sign offsets to distinguish symmetry breaking from matching a trained distribution.
Report a crossed base-initializer-by-proposed-initializer table when the standard baseline recipe is changed.
Measure activation distributions and gradients alongside accuracy to turn a surprising heuristic into a mechanism.
A negative structural observation, such as useless W1/W2 anticorrelation, is valuable because visually prominent trained statistics need not be causally useful.
Publish exact plot data for small initialization effects, since rounding and visual extraction can be comparable to the effect itself.
open_questions: Does Eq. 1, with a random per-network group mean and zero global population mean, outperform Eq. 2 under a fully reported large-scale comparison?
What b and sigma were used for each reported curve, and how sensitive are results after jointly tuning learning rate and weight decay?
Are the Figure 1 heatmaps centered covariances, correlations, or uncentered second moments?
Does a hierarchical random-effects model quantitatively explain the striped population covariance?
Does sampling the scalar b randomly with mean zero retain the gain while actually creating cross-entry covariance?
Is the operative mechanism symmetry breaking, a common feature proportional to sum(x), altered activation sparsity, or better gradient conditioning?
How does the method interact with GELU versus ReLU, pre-norm versus post-norm, biases, and centered inputs?
Does the effect persist when compute rather than epochs is matched and when training reaches equal loss?
How does benefit scale with dataset size, width, depth, expansion ratio, and number of independently trained source models?
Can an entry alignment that makes W1/W2 cross-covariance meaningful be specified and tested without dimension ambiguity?
Does the method help language MLPs, MLP-Mixers, pure MLPs, or normalization-free networks?
How does it compare against GradInit, MetaInit, Fixup, IDInit, and scale-unbalanced initialization under identical budgets?
Are trained-weight stripes stable across seeds, layers, checkpoints, optimizers, and architectures, or are they induced by parameter symmetries?
Can the endpoint ImageNet gain be replicated with enough seeds to resolve a 0.4-point effect and its uncertainty?

competitive_landscape.title: IDInit: A Universal and Stable Initialization Method for Neural Network Training
competitive_landscape.relationship: A recent direct initialization competitor that targets faster, stable training across deep models.
competitive_landscape.difference: IDInit constructs padded identity-like matrices and supplies dynamical-isometry/convergence motivation; this paper instead adds a scalar mean to W1 based on a qualitative statistic of trained MLP weights and does not compare against IDInit.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2025 Poster, OpenReview forum LFiaoYnP6T, last modified 2025-04-02

competitive_landscape.title: GradInit: Learning to Initialize Neural Networks for Stable and Efficient Training
competitive_landscape.relationship: A direct architecture-agnostic competitor for accelerating early optimization through initialization.
competitive_landscape.difference: GradInit optimizes a scalar multiplier for each parameter block so one prescribed optimizer step lowers loss; it is data- and optimizer-aware but incurs an initialization optimization, whereas the reviewed method is closed-form, changes a first moment, and is motivated by trained-weight geometry.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34, NeurIPS 2021 official proceedings edition

competitive_landscape.title: MetaInit: Initializing learning by learning to initialize
competitive_landscape.relationship: A direct learned-initialization baseline focused on making early gradient descent locally easier.
competitive_landscape.difference: MetaInit minimizes a gradient quotient by tuning layer norms and evaluates deep plain/ResNet training; it does not use pretrained weight populations or introduce a nonzero W1 mean, but it provides a missing automated baseline for the same trainability claim.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32, NeurIPS 2019 official proceedings edition

competitive_landscape.title: Fixup Initialization: Residual Learning Without Normalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: A canonical hand-designed initialization competitor that accelerates and stabilizes deep residual training.
competitive_landscape.difference: Fixup derives depth-dependent residual-branch scaling and zero-initialized components to control updates without normalization; it is architecture-specific and theory-motivated rather than learned from population covariance, and it does not test a channel-MLP mean shift.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2019 published conference paper, OpenReview forum H1gsz30cKX

competitive_landscape.title: Get rich quick: exact solutions reveal how unbalanced initializations promote rapid feature learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: A mechanistic competitor for the claim that simple departures from standard balanced initialization can speed useful feature learning.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies layer-specific variance and learning-rate imbalance with exact dynamics in tractable models and deep-network experiments; the reviewed paper changes a mean based on trained-weight statistics, supplies no dynamics, and cites but does not experimentally compare this explanation.

competitive_landscape.title: Mimetic Initialization of Self-Attention Layers
competitive_landscape.relationship: The closest published methodological antecedent and same-author mimetic-initialization lineage.
competitive_landscape.difference: The ICML paper initializes correlated query/key and anticorrelated value/projection products plus positional structure, reporting final gains over 4-5 points; the reviewed paper targets channel-mixing W1 with a scalar shift and mostly transient, much smaller gains.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202:34456-34468, published 2023-07-03

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding the Covariance Structure of Convolutional Filters
competitive_landscape.relationship: A same-author direct antecedent that turns trained convolutional covariance into a learning-free multivariate initializer.
competitive_landscape.difference: It models spatial-filter covariance and tests transfer across convolutional architectures; the reviewed paper extends the observational recipe to channel-mixing MLPs but reduces the intervention to a first-moment shift whose covariance interpretation is problematic.

competitive_landscape.title: Mimetic Initialization Helps State Space Models Learn to Recall
competitive_landscape.relationship: A same-author antecedent applying mimetic structure to another layer family and explicitly measuring training acceleration.
competitive_landscape.difference: It makes Mamba state-space layers approximate attention to solve copying and recall failures, with targeted synthetic mechanisms; the reviewed method operates on generic vision MLP W1 and offers no analogous task-level mechanism.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first application of mimetic initialization to channel-mixing MLP layers, using a small nonzero mean in the first MLP weight matrix to speed CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1k training and to complement spatial-mixing initializers.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper estimates joint MLP-weight covariance across whole trained-network populations, proposes two closed-form broadcast offsets, and reports early gains in ConvNeXt and ViT plus a 68.8% versus 68.4% 100-epoch ImageNet endpoint. Its related work documents earlier mimetic initializers only for convolution, self-attention, and state-space layers.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The narrow layer-family extension and population-as-samples analysis are plausibly novel, but the demonstrated contribution is best described as a preliminary scalar-mean heuristic rather than a validated covariance-mimicking method. A fixed scalar shift cannot generate centered covariance stripes, the main hyperparameters are missing, gains largely fade, and strong independent initialization competitors are not tested. Novelty confidence is therefore higher than mechanism or empirical-strength confidence.

reviewer_notes: Read all five extracted pages end to end; the paper has no appendix. Source hashes, page count, and locator were copied exactly from fulltext_index.jsonl. Figures 2-4 were also inspected in the cached PDF because extraction omitted axes and curves. Numbers labeled approximate are visual readings; the only exact large-scale endpoint in prose is 68.8% versus 68.4%. Competitor identities, titles, and editions were checked on official OpenReview, NeurIPS/PMLR proceedings, and arXiv pages on 2026-08-23. The strongest audit boundary is that Eq. 2 changes a mean but not centered population covariance; this is reviewer algebra, not an author admission.
